problem.3: Following leading clinical research: You don't have to live with bloating, constipation or gas.
problem.4: The 3pm meeting. The belt let out by dinner. Mornings you cannot plan. In an international survey of more than 73,000 adults across 33 countries, conducted online in most of them, more than 40% met the criteria for at least one functional gut problem. It is common. It is not normal. And it is rarely fixed by a capsule that opens in the wrong place.
problem.8: Wind you have to plan around.
problem.10: Going every morning should not be a surprise.
problem.14: Fine for a week, then chaos.
problem.15: 70 billion live cultures, eight named strains, clinically studied postbiotic, delayed-release capsule, scientist formulated, no fridge, vegan
science.3: Gleev was developed by Tim Verhaeghe, who leads medical and regulatory at Gleev, as a four-part system rather than a single ingredient. Every strain and ingredient was chosen for what the research on it shows.
science.6: Leads medical and regulatory at Gleev
science.7: With decades of experience formulating exceptional health products, Tim collaborated with our scientific gut health team to develop Gleev: an all-in-one solution designed to support a truly healthy gut.
science.8: Developed by a scientist, not fronted by a face.
science.10: L. reuteri: a strain family studied for how the gut moves.
science.11: The species has been studied in humans for bowel movement frequency, functional constipation, abdominal pain and discomfort, and as an adjunct in H. pylori therapy: eight randomised controlled trials, 1,087 patients.
science.12: Li 2024; reviews Mu 2018, Peng 2023. Strain-family level.
science.13: L. paracasei: studied for bloating, wind and stool form.
science.14: The species has been studied in humans for bloating, flatulence, stool form and stool frequency, including hard or lumpy stools.
science.15: Compare 2015; Cook 2025; Lahner 2011; Cremon 2018. Strain-family level.
science.17: One of the most studied probiotic strains in the world.
science.18: Meta-analyses in acute gastroenteritis (18 randomised controlled trials, more than 4,000 children) and antibiotic-associated diarrhoea; mechanisms of mucus adhesion and barrier support.
science.21: A postbiotic with randomised, placebo-controlled trials and decades in French pharmacies.
science.22: Humiome® Post LB: five double-blind placebo-controlled paediatric trials in acute diarrhoea; a 137-adult randomised trial in chronic diarrhoea; a 325-patient study on antibiotic-associated diarrhoea; IBS research including a 297-patient IBS-D study. Sold as a licensed medicine in French pharmacies for decades.
science.23: Salazar-Lindo 2007; Xiao 2003; Tarrerias 2011; Halpern 1996; Warda 2021. Ingredient level.
journey.2: The journey through your stomach matters.
journey.3: A fasted stomach is about as acidic as battery acid. Most capsules open there. Gleev's delayed-release capsule stayed intact for over an hour in acid of that strength, in laboratory testing, so its contents are carried further down before release.
journey.4: Illustration of a stomach and intestine with the text: Targeted release. Right where it matters.

how.3: Most gut supplements stop at two.
how.9: The delayed-release capsule carries everything past the stomach.
how.10: 100mg of chicory inulin reaches the colon and feeds the bacteria you want more of, and helps the cultures stay robust on the way.
how.11: 70 billion live cultures across eight named strains, at the amounts on the label.
how.12: 170mg of a postbiotic that works on the gut whether or not anything survives, with a medical track record.

inside.2: Inside the capsule. Every strain, every amount, every job.
inside.3: Eight named strains with their codes and amounts. A postbiotic with its deposit numbers. A prebiotic. Vitamin B2. A plant-based delayed-release capsule. Every batch tested. We print every strain and every amount. Ask your probiotic to do the same.
inside.13: Chosen for how your gut moves and how it feels. Relevant to bowel movement frequency and abdominal comfort.
inside.14: Strain family studied in 8 RCTs, 1,087 patients (Li 2024).
inside.18: Chosen for bloating, wind and stool form, including hard or lumpy stools.
inside.19: Strain family studied for bloating, flatulence, stool form and frequency (Compare 2015; Cook 2025).
inside.24: Resilience when your gut is knocked sideways. One of the most studied probiotic strains in the world.
inside.25: Meta-analyses in acute gastroenteritis and antibiotic-associated diarrhoea (Szajewska 2015, 2019).
inside.29: The bifidobacterium that eats the fibre we feed it. Relevant to the colon, comfort and bowel function.
inside.30: Species studied in IBS for pain, bloating and permeability; in chronic constipation for stool consistency (Bonfrate 2020; Srivastava 2024).
inside.34: A named Bifidobacterium strain at a printed amount, broadening the formula across both families.
inside.study.lactis: Species studied for improved bowel regularity and in IBS for reduced abdominal pain, bloating and improved bowel habits (Eskesen 2015; Martoni 2020).
inside.study.bifidum: Species studied in IBS, with clinical research reporting relief from abdominal pain, bloating and urgency, alongside improved digestive comfort and quality of life (Guglielmetti 2011; Andresen 2020).
inside.study.plantarum: Species studied in IBS, with clinical research demonstrating improvements in abdominal pain, bloating and overall digestive comfort (Ducrotté 2012).
inside.study.acidophilus: Species studied in IBS, with clinical research reporting reductions in abdominal pain and bloating, alongside improvements in bowel habits and digestive comfort (Martoni 2020).
inside.40: A named Lactobacillus strain at a printed amount, broadening the formula across both families.
inside.47: A defined, heat-treated preparation of L. fermentum CNCM I-2998 and L. delbrueckii CNCM I-4831 with their fermentation matrix. Works whether or not anything survives the journey.
inside.48: Sold as a licensed medicine in French pharmacies for decades.
inside.51: Five double-blind placebo-controlled paediatric trials in acute diarrhoea; a 137-adult randomised trial in chronic diarrhoea; a 325-patient study on antibiotic-associated diarrhoea; a 297-patient IBS-D study and a randomised crossover trial.
inside.54: The part your probiotic does not have
inside.55: Mechanism work shows adhesion to intestinal cells, inhibition of pathogen adhesion, protection of tight junctions and a bifidogenic effect.
inside.56: Warda 2021. Research on the postbiotic preparation.
inside.59: A fibre that resists digestion and reaches the colon, where it is selectively used by bifidobacteria, including the three in this capsule.
inside.63: In formulation studies inulin improved the viability and stress tolerance of lactobacilli, including LGG, under simulated gut stress and in storage. The fibre looks after the cultures before they get to work.
inside.67: Vitamin B2 contributes to the maintenance of normal mucous membranes.
inside.71: A clear vegetarian capsule of gellan gum and pectin, specified to resist disintegration for more than 30 minutes.
inside.74: Acid-resistance test reports show the capsule intact for over 60 minutes in 0.1M hydrochloric acid, about pH 1, the acid strength of a fasted stomach.
inside.75: A laboratory test on the capsule. Not a human outcome.
inside.78: Contents are carried past the stomach and released further down, where the cultures, fibre and postbiotic are meant to work.
inside.81: Every batch tested for microbial contaminants and heavy metals (not more than 10ppm).
inside.84: No GM material. Not irradiated. 56 capsules, 28 days, two a day.
inside.87: Two capsules with your first glass of water. That is the whole routine.

faq.5: The ingredients, strains and capsule are. The two lead strain families have published human research on bloating, stool form and bowel movement; LGG is one of the most studied probiotic strains in the world; the postbiotic has randomised, placebo-controlled trials and has been sold as a medicine in French pharmacies for decades; the capsule has been tested in stomach-strength acid.
faq.7: Because 70 billion cultures, 170mg of postbiotic and 100mg of fibre do not fit in one. Two with your first glass of water is the whole routine.
faq.8: What if I feel nothing in week two?
faq.9: Month one is arrival. Months two and three are where it becomes a foundation. Nothing dramatic in the first fortnight is normal. If something is wrong, speak to a doctor.
